finalReport.rawFindings:
--- CRITICAL FINDINGS ---

[DB-1] Unbounded user trade fetch (no pagination)
File: actions/trade.ts (L200-L360)
Evidence: getAllTrades and getTradeStats call prisma.tradeLog.findMany({ where: { userId: ... } }) (no take/limit/cursor) and include pyramids/exits, returning all rows for a user in one request. This issues a full read of a growing table and loads related children in the same request.
Impact: At modest scale (hundreds of users or a single user with >10k trades) this will cause huge query latency and DB IOPS; under 10x QPS this will degrade from ms → seconds and can make pages time out for many users simultaneously.  
Fix: Add cursor/limit pagination (or a time/range filter) and limit includes; provide lightweight summary endpoints and load details lazily.

[DB-2] Financial multi-step writes not wrapped in transactions
File: actions/trade-pyramid.ts (L1-L220) and actions/trade.ts (L1-L200)
Evidence: createTradePyramid/createTrade (and likely createTradeExit) perform multiple DB writes (create pyramid/trade, then create fund entries, then recalc status/avg) as separate awaits without prisma.$transaction wrapping them. Fund creation errors are caught and ignored, leaving partial commits.
Impact: Concurrent failures or partial errors will leave inconsistent financial state (missing fund rows, wrong displayQuantity/status) and can corrupt P&L and billing flows; with concurrent writes this leads to data inconsistency at <100 concurrent write operations.  
Fix: Wrap related writes in a single DB transaction (Prisma $transaction) with short critical sections, and make compensating operations explicit when external calls are involved.

[DB-3] Write hotspot + sequential recalculations causing contention
File: actions/trade-pyramid.ts (L1-L220)
Evidence: After creating/deleting/updating a pyramid the code calls recalculateTradeStatus and recalculateAverageEntryPrice which update the same TradeLog row, performed synchronously per change (no batching). Multiple simultaneous pyramids/exits update the same trade row repeatedly.
Impact: Under concurrent exits/pyramids to the same trade this causes row-level contention and increased lock waits, causing degraded latency and failed requests at tens of simultaneous conflicting writes.  
Fix: Shorten transactions, move expensive recalculations to background jobs (enqueue) or use optimized single transactional queries that update aggregates atomically.

--- WARNING FINDINGS ---

[DB-4] Missing index for queries filtered only by userId
File: prisma/schema.prisma (TradeLog model, L1-L70)
Evidence: TradeLog has compound indexes like [userId, profileId, status] and [userId, profileId, date] but no single or [userId,date] index; code often queries by { userId } alone (getAllTrades/getTradeStats). 
Impact: Queries that filter by userId alone will do broader index scans/table scans as the trade table grows, increasing DB CPU/IOPS and causing slow responses at tens of thousands of rows per user.  
Fix: Add an index on userId (or userId + date) or ensure application always queries with a profileId or a paginated cursor.

[DB-5] Serverless connection risk despite singleton Prisma client
File: src/lib/prisma.ts (L1-L40)
Evidence: The code correctly uses a global singleton PrismaClient (good), but DATABASE_URL/pooler configuration or external pooler (pgbouncer) is not present in repo; serverless deployments still spawn many instances that each open DB connections.
Impact: At high QPS with many concurrent server instances you can still exhaust DB connections or hit connection churn — symptoms at tens–low-hundreds of concurrent instances (connection exhaustion, auth failures).  
Fix: Use a connection pooler (pgbouncer/proxy) or a serverless-friendly pool (connection limits via DATABASE_URL), and keep Prisma singleton; also cap concurrency and prefer background workers for heavy work.

[DB-6] Bulk import and per-row synchronous writes amplify DB load
File: actions/trade.ts (bulkImportTrades) (L300-L520)
Evidence: bulkImportTrades processes many rows sequentially and calls createTradePyramid/addTrade/createTradeExit for each row, each making multiple DB writes and recalculations synchronously.  
Impact: Importing large files can generate thousands of sequential writes and recalculations, causing high DB write IOPS, lock contention, and long request durations (timeouts) — this can saturate DB under high concurrent imports.  
Fix: Convert bulk import to batched transactions, use bulk inserts where possible, or run import as an async job with controlled concurrency and batched processing.

--- INFO ---

[DB-7] Prisma + PostgreSQL + many indexes present
File: prisma/schema.prisma
Evidence: Schema uses PostgreSQL datasource, Prisma client, and several targeted compound indexes (LivePrice, DailyClose, Fund, DailyReport, etc.).  
Use INFO only: schema already includes many useful indexes (e.g., LivePrice unique/index on [symbol,exchange,segment]), which reduces risk for those specific lookups.
